body.objective: Students will be able to define psychology and its perspectives.
body.iCan: I can define psychology and its perspectives.
successCriteria: I can define psychology and explain why it is a science
I can describe the major perspectives in psychology
I can tell the difference between psychology and pop psychology
body.hook: Why do people procrastinate? Why do we remember embarrassing moments so clearly? Why do some people stay calm under pressure? Everyone has theories about human behaviour, but psychology tests those ideas with evidence. That's what makes it a science.

vocabulary.definition: The scientific study of behaviour and mental processes.
Actions that can be observed, such as speaking, moving or eating.
Inner experiences such as thinking, feeling, remembering and dreaming.
A way of explaining behaviour that focuses on certain causes.
Information gained through observation and measurement.
Claims presented as scientific without real evidence.

study.title: Six Ways to Explain Behaviour
study.question: What is psychology, and how do psychologists explain behaviour?
study.passage:
Major perspectives:
• Biological: behaviour is shaped by the brain, nervous system, hormones and genes.
• Behavioural: behaviour is learned through rewards, punishments and experience.
• Cognitive: behaviour depends on how we think, remember and solve problems.
• Humanistic: people have free will and are motivated to grow and reach their potential.
• Psychodynamic: unconscious thoughts and early experiences influence behaviour (based on Freud; many ideas are now debated).
• Sociocultural: culture, family and society shape behaviour.
Case: Jordan, 16, procrastinates on every major assignment, then stays up all night before the deadline.
Explain Jordan's behaviour through each perspective. Example (biological): the teenage prefrontal cortex, which helps with planning and impulse control, is still developing.
Pop psychology check: Rate these claims as supported by evidence, mixed, or unsupported:
1. "People only use 10% of their brains."
2. "Sleep affects memory."
3. "You're either left-brained or right-brained."
4. "Exercise can improve mood."
Science answer: 1 and 3 are myths; 2 and 4 are supported by research.
study.source: Original case written for this lesson; perspectives summarized from introductory psychology sources.
steps: Explain the case through each perspective
Discuss what makes psychology a science
discussion: Which perspective best explains Jordan's procrastination? Why?
Why is the "10% of the brain" claim a myth?
study.product: Choose a common behaviour (for example, stage fright or phone addiction) and explain it through three perspectives, then evaluate one pop-psychology claim about it using evidence.

examples.title: Behaviour vs mental process
examples.problem: Is "remembering a phone number" a behaviour or mental process?
examples.explore: Give an example of a behaviour.

examples.title: Behavioural perspective
examples.problem: How would a behaviourist explain Jordan?
examples.answer: Last-minute work has been rewarded with passing grades, so the habit continues

examples.title: Cognitive perspective
examples.problem: How would a cognitive psychologist explain Jordan?
examples.answer: He may underestimate how long tasks take or think "I work best under pressure"
examples.explore: How could he change his thinking?

examples.title: Pseudoscience
examples.problem: Why is "left-brained vs right-brained" a myth?
examples.answer: Both hemispheres work together in nearly all tasks; people aren't one "type"
